mechanical-pencil.context: A slim pencil drawn at an angle with a push cap, a pocket clip and a thin lead showing at the tip. Used for drafting, school supplies and writing tools.

click-pen.context: A retractable ballpoint pen with a plunger button on top, a side clip and a small tip. Used for writing, signing and office supplies.

multicolor-pen.context: A chunky pen with several colour slider tabs along one side and a single writing tip. Used for note taking, planners and school supplies.

dip-pen.context: A holder with a pointed split metal nib angled for writing, with a small breather hole in the nib. Used for calligraphy, lettering and old style writing.

inkwell.context: A squat square glass ink bottle with a short neck and a visible ink level, with a pen resting in the neck. Used for calligraphy, writing and traditional stationery.

ink-blot.context: An irregular ink splash with a rounded middle and a few droplets scattered around it. Used for spills, stains, messy writing and Rorschach style tests.

pencil-box.context: An open hard case with its lid raised at the back and two pencils lying inside compartments. Used for school supplies, art kits and desk organisers.

pencil-roll.context: A rolled out fabric wrap with a row of slots, three pencils standing in the slots and a tie cord. Used for art supplies, drawing kits and carrying pencils.

pencil-cup.context: A desk cup holding three pens and pencils sticking out at different angles. Used for desk organisers, offices and writing supplies.

desk-pen-set.context: A rectangular desk base with a small holder and a slim pen angled upward out of it. Used for executive gifts, reception desks and formal signing.

crank-pencil-sharpener.context: A desk sharpener with a round body, a pencil hole in front and a side crank ending in a knob. Used in classrooms and offices for sharpening pencils.

correction-tape.context: A handheld oval tape dispenser with a pointed applicator tip laying a white strip. Used for covering mistakes in handwriting and printed text.

correction-fluid.context: A small bottle with its screw cap lifted above the neck, the cap carrying a brush. Used for painting over mistakes on paper.

whiteboard-eraser.context: A rectangular eraser block with a curved grip on top and a felt pad along the bottom. Used for wiping whiteboards and chalkboards in classrooms and meetings.

pen-refill.context: A long thin ink tube with a pointed tip and a small spring coiled near the tip end. Used for replacing the ink cartridge in a ballpoint pen.

pencil-lead-refill.context: A slim tube with a sliding cap and two thin lead sticks visible inside. Used for refilling mechanical pencils.

rocker-blotter.context: A curved rocker base covered in blotting paper with a round knob on top. Used for soaking up wet ink after writing with a dip pen or fountain pen.

wax-seal.context: A round wax disc with irregular melted edges and a star pressed into the middle. Used for sealing letters, invitations and official documents.

wax-seal-stamp.context: A turned wooden handle with a round metal head standing above a small wax puddle. Used for pressing a design into melted wax on letters and invitations.

ink-pad.context: A flat tin with its lid open, showing a soaked pad inside. Used for inking rubber stamps and fingerprints.

date-stamp.context: A rubber stamp with a loop handle, a number band on its body and a flat base plate. Used for marking received dates on paperwork and mail.

seal-embosser.context: A C-shaped hand press with a die between its jaws, used to raise a seal on paper. Used by notaries, schools and companies for certificates.

padfolio.context: An open writing folio with a notepad on the right half and card pockets on the left. Used for meetings, interviews and conferences.

legal-pad.context: A tall writing pad with a thick binding strip across the top, a margin line and ruled lines. Used for notes, drafts and legal work.

steno-pad.context: A narrow notepad with spiral rings along the top and a line splitting the page into two columns. Used for shorthand, interviews and quick notes.

composition-notebook.context: A notebook with a speckled cover, a dark spine strip and a small blank label box. Used for school work, journals and class notes.

index-card.context: A horizontal card with a heading line near the top and several ruled lines below it. Used for flash cards, recipes, study notes and cue cards.

index-card-box.context: A small open box of upright index cards with a tabbed divider sticking up. Used for recipe files, flash cards and card catalogs.

graph-paper.context: A sheet covered in a square grid with the top right corner folded down. Used for maths, plotting, engineering sketches and pixel art.

loose-leaf-paper.context: A ruled sheet with three punched holes and a margin line on the left. Used for school notes, homework and binders.

dot-grid-paper.context: A sheet with evenly spaced dots in rows and columns and a folded corner. Used for bullet journals, sketching, lettering and planning.

tractor-feed-paper.context: Continuous fan folded paper with sprocket holes along both edges and a fold below. Used for old computer printouts and dot matrix printers.

paper-ream.context: A wrapped pack of paper with a label on the front and a sheet edge showing on top. Used for office printing supplies and bulk paper orders.

thermal-paper-roll.context: A paper roll on its spool with the loose end hanging down as a receipt strip. Used for receipt printers, tills and card readers.

letterhead.context: A sheet of paper with a header band holding a small emblem and a line of text, with lines of text below. Used for company letters and official correspondence.

folded-letter.context: A letter folded in three with two crease lines and a short line of handwriting on the middle panel. Used for mail, notices and correspondence.

crumpled-paper.context: A ball of crushed paper with jagged creases and folded facets. Used for discarded drafts, waste, mistakes and lost ideas.

memo-cube.context: A thick cube of loose note sheets seen from a corner with sheet edges on its sides. Used for desk notes, reminders and quick messages.

page-flags.context: The edge of a page with a row of narrow index flags sticking out of its side. Used for marking pages in books, contracts and documents for review.

label-sheet.context: A sheet with a grid of rounded labels, the last one peeling at the corner. Used for address labels, stickers and printing labels.

shipping-label.context: A rectangular label with address lines at the top and a barcode strip at the bottom. Used for parcels, couriers and postage.

planner.context: An open spiral-bound planner with two facing pages split into small day boxes. Used for schedules, appointments and weekly planning.

desk-calendar.context: A tent-shaped standing calendar with rings across the top and a date grid on its front. Used on office desks for dates and schedules.

tear-off-calendar.context: A calendar pad with a large day number on the top sheet and a jagged torn strip above it. Used for daily calendars hung on walls and kitchens.

perpetual-calendar.context: Two small number cubes on a stand above a block showing the month. Used as a desk date display that you turn by hand.

timesheet.context: A grid form with a small clock face in its header, used for logging hours worked. Used for payroll, attendance and billing.

time-card.context: A tall narrow punch card with a notch at the top, a name line and two columns of time stamps. Used for clocking in and out at a time clock.

punched-card.context: A card with one clipped corner and rows of small rectangular holes punched across it. Used as a symbol of early computing and data storage.

brochure.context: A tri-fold leaflet opened into three panels, with an image block and text marks. Used for marketing, travel guides and handouts.

flyer.context: A portrait sheet with a large picture block, a bold title bar and short text lines. Used for event posters, handbills and announcements.

resume.context: A portrait document with a round portrait at the top left, a name line and stacked sections of text. Used for job applications and career profiles.

sketchbook.context: A book with a spiral along the top edge and a simple mountain doodle on the page. Used for drawing, doodling and art practice.

elastic-band-notebook.context: A hardcover notebook closed by a vertical elastic strap, with a ribbon bookmark hanging below. Used for journals, planners and note taking.

paper-spike.context: An upright metal spike on a weighted base with several receipts pierced on it. Used in diners, kitchens and shops to hold order slips and bills.

padded-envelope.context: An envelope with a flap strip and a pattern of small bubbles on the front. Used for mailing fragile or small items.

window-envelope.context: A long envelope with a clear address window on the left and a stamp square on the right. Used for bills, invoices and bank statements.

clasp-envelope.context: A large portrait envelope with a pointed flap held down by a round metal clasp. Used for documents, catalogs and larger papers.

interoffice-envelope.context: A portrait envelope with two button discs joined by string and a routing grid on the front. Used for reusable internal mail inside offices.

airmail-envelope.context: An envelope with diagonal stripes along the bottom edge and a stamp in the top corner. Used for international letters and overseas post.

letter-opener.context: A slim pointed blade with a rounded handle, its tip slid under the top edge of an envelope. Used for opening mail cleanly at a desk.

postmark.context: A circular cancellation ring with a date line inside and wavy lines trailing to the right. Used for post office marks on stamped letters.

post-horn.context: A coiled horn with a flared bell and a small mouthpiece, the old sign of postal services. Used for post offices, mail couriers and delivery.

stamp-sheet.context: A sheet of postage stamps in a three by three grid with perforated gaps between them. Used for stamp collecting and buying postage.

po-box.context: A wall of small post office box doors, two across and three down, each with a tiny knob. Used for private mailboxes rented at a post office.

parcel-locker.context: A wall unit of lockers in several sizes with a small screen and a keypad panel on the left. Used for self service parcel pickup and drop off.

mail-sack.context: A canvas sack cinched at the neck with a ruffled top and an envelope on its front. Used for bulk letters carried by postal workers.

mail-cart.context: A wheeled cart with a deep bin, a push handle on one side and letters stacked above the bin. Used for moving mail around an office or mail room.

mail-sorting-rack.context: A grid of open pigeonhole slots with envelopes tucked into some of the compartments. Used for sorting mail by recipient in offices and post rooms.

postage-meter.context: A desk postage machine with a display and a slot, with an envelope sliding out below carrying a printed mark. Used for stamping mail in offices.

letter-scale.context: A small desk scale with a curved dial and an envelope resting on its plate. Used for weighing letters to work out postage.

parcel-scale.context: A flat weighing platform with a box on it and a separate display unit joined by a cord. Used for weighing parcels before shipping.

suggestion-box.context: A closed box with a slot in its lid and a folded note being dropped into the slot. Used for collecting feedback, ideas and complaints.

mailing-tube.context: A long cardboard tube with round end caps and a label band around the middle. Used for posting posters, drawings and rolled documents.

bubble-wrap.context: A sheet of plastic covered in round air bubbles with a big curled corner. Used for protecting fragile items in boxes and parcels.

packing-peanuts.context: A small pile of curved S-shaped foam packing pieces. Used for cushioning items inside shipping boxes.

tape-gun.context: A packing tape dispenser with a pistol grip, a tape roll on top and a toothed cutter at the front. Used for sealing boxes quickly.

stretch-film.context: A roll of plastic wrap on a hand core with a wide sheet unrolling from it. Used for wrapping pallets, boxes and furniture.

string-tied-parcel.context: A paper wrapped parcel tied with twine crossing both ways and knotted at the middle. Used for old style packages and posted gifts.

doorstep-parcel.context: A taped box sitting on a doormat in front of the bottom of a closed door. Used for delivered packages and porch drop offs.

parcel-handover.context: An open hand held out from below carrying a small taped box. Used for hand delivery, receiving parcels and signed for delivery.
